question: How do the I-part and this-part relate to each other in cognition?
premises: The I-part and the this-part arise together in cognition.
Each part excludes the other in its own functioning.
The I-part can conceal the this-part within its own domain.
inference: The I and this aspects of experience are mutually exclusive yet dynamically related within the same cognition.
plain_english: These two parts mutually exclude each other; the own 'I' conceals the 'this' part, which stands in cognition, within its own 'I'-aspect.
